unexpected-inflation.def: Inflation different from what people anticipated when they signed loans, wage contracts or pensions. Unanticipated inflation redistributes purchasing power; anticipated inflation is built into those agreements.

fixed-income.def: An income set in dollars that does not rise with prices, such as a pension that pays the same amount each month. Unanticipated inflation hurts people on fixed incomes and lenders and helps fixed-rate borrowers.

menu-costs.def: The costs to firms of changing prices often, such as reprinting menus and updating price tags. Shoe-leather costs are the time and effort people spend holding less cash when inflation erodes its value.
